238: static void sdio_dma_rx_start(dma_id_t id)
239: {
240: 	if(id != s_sdio_host.dma_rx_id)
241: 	{
242: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGW("%s:id=%d,sdio_id=%d\r\n", __func__, id, s_sdio_host.dma_rx_id);
243: 		return;
244: 	}
245: 
246: 	if(s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len >= s_sdio_host.rx_total_len)
247: 	{
248: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGV("%s:id=%d,total_len=%d,transfered_len=%d\r\n", __func__, id, s_sdio_host.rx_total_len, s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len);
249: 		return;
250: 	}
251: 
252: 	uint32_t remain_len = s_sdio_host.rx_total_len - s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len;
253: 	uint32_t next_trans_len = remain_len < bk_dma_get_transfer_len_max(id) ? remain_len : bk_dma_get_transfer_len_max(id);
254: 
255: 	if(next_trans_len)
256: 	{
257: 		s_sdio_host.rx_cur_trans_len = next_trans_len;
258: 		bk_dma_set_transfer_len(id, next_trans_len);
259: 		bk_dma_set_dest_addr(id, (uint32_t)(s_sdio_host.rx_start_addr + s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len), (uint32_t)((s_sdio_host.rx_start_addr + s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len)+next_trans_len));
260: 		bk_dma_start(id);
261: 	}
262: }

264: void sdio_dma_rx_finish(dma_id_t id)
265: {
266: 	static uint32_t s_dma_rx_finish_cnt = 0;
267: 
268: 	s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len += s_sdio_host.rx_cur_trans_len;	//Current round finish, add the transfered len
269: 	sdio_dma_rx_start(id);
270: 
271: 	if(s_sdio_host.rx_total_len <= s_sdio_host.rx_transfered_len)
272: 	{
273: 		rtos_set_semaphore(&s_sdio_host.rx_sema);
274: 		s_dma_rx_finish_cnt++;
275: 		SDIO_HOST_LOGV("%s:s_dma_rx_finish_cnt=%d\r\n", __func__, s_dma_rx_finish_cnt);
276: 	}
277: }

113: static isr_t* int_isr_del(icu_int_src_t src)
114: {
115: 
116: 	LIST_HEADER_T *pos, *next;
117: 
118: 	isr_t *cur_ptr;
119: 	isr_list_t *int_list;
120: 
121: 	// icu_int_map_t icu_int_map_table[] = ICU_DEV_MAP;
122: 	if (src >= ARRAY_SIZE(icu_int_map_table)) {
123: 		ICU_LOGW("int_isr_del, int_src(%d) is out of icu_int_map_table range\r\n", src);
124: 		return NULL;
125: 	}
126: 	const icu_int_map_t *icu_int_map = &icu_int_map_table[src];
127: 
128: 	uint32_t int_num = icu_int_map->int_bit;
129: 	uint32_t group_id = icu_int_map->group;
130: 
131: 	int_list = &s_int_lists[group_id];
132: 
133: 	ICU_LOGV("delete:src: %d pri=tem_ptr->pri, int_num = %d\r\n", src, int_num);
134: 	GLOBAL_INT_DECLARATION();
135: 
136: 	GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
137: 	if (list_empty(&int_list->isr)) {
138: 		GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
139: 		return NULL;
140: 	}
141: 
142: 	list_for_each_safe(pos, next, &int_list->isr) {
143: 		cur_ptr = list_entry(pos, isr_t, list);
144: 
145: 		if (int_num == cur_ptr->int_num) {
146: 			ICU_LOGV("delete:src: %d pri=tem_ptr->pri, int_num = %d\r\n", src, int_num);
147: 			list_del(&cur_ptr->list);
148: 			GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
149: 			return cur_ptr;
150: 		}
151: 	}
152: 
153: 	GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
154: 
155: 	return NULL;
156: }

162: 	if (cur_isr) {

169: bk_err_t int_isr_add(isr_t *new_isr, int group_id)
170: {
171: 	LIST_HEADER_T *pos, *next;
172: 	isr_t *cur_ptr;
173: 	isr_list_t *int_list;
174: 
175: 	int_list = &s_int_lists[group_id];
176: 
177: 	GLOBAL_INT_DECLARATION();
178: 	GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
179: 	if (list_empty(&int_list->isr)) {
180: 		list_add_head(&new_isr->list, &int_list->isr);
181: 		goto int_isr_add_exit;
182: 	}
183: 
184: 	/* Insert the ISR to the function list, this list is sorted by priority number */
185: 	list_for_each_safe(pos, next, &int_list->isr) {
186: 		cur_ptr = list_entry(pos, isr_t, list);
187: 
188: 		ICU_LOGV("cur isr: num = %d, pri=%d\n", cur_ptr->int_num, cur_ptr->pri);
189: 		if (new_isr->pri <= cur_ptr->pri) {
190: 			/* add entry at the head of the queue */
191: 			ICU_LOGV("add new isr: num = %d, pri=%d\n", new_isr->int_num, new_isr->pri);
192: 			list_add_tail(&new_isr->list, &cur_ptr->list);
193: 			goto int_isr_add_exit;
194: 		}
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	list_add_tail(&new_isr->list, &int_list->isr);
198: 	ICU_LOGV("add new isr: num = %d, pri=%d\n", new_isr->int_num, new_isr->pri);
199: 
200: int_isr_add_exit:
201: 	s_isr_mask[group_id] |= BIT(new_isr->int_num);
202: 	GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
203: 
204: 	return BK_OK;
205: }

221: 	uint8_t int_pri = icu_int_map->int_prio;
222: 	uint8_t group_id = icu_int_map->group;
223: 	isr_t *new_isr;
224: 
225: 	ICU_LOGV("register isr: src=%d, num=%d, pri=%d, group=%d\r\n", src, int_num, int_pri, group_id );
226: 	new_isr = (isr_t*)os_malloc(sizeof(isr_t));
227: 	if(!new_isr) {
228: 		ICU_LOGE("cur_ptr malloc error\r\n");
229: 		return BK_ERR_NO_MEM;

564: ### 6.3 IRQ
565: 
566: BK7258 AP IRQ表来源：
567: 
568: - `bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/icu_map.h:28-94`
569: - `bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/bk7258_ap/interrupt.c:114-245`
570: 
571: 已确认的外部NVIC line：
572: 
573: | 外设 | 外部line | NuttX IRQ |
574: | --- | ---: | ---: |
575: | TIMER0 | 3 | 19 |
576: | UART0 | 4 | 20 |
577: | TIMER1 | 13 | 29 |
578: | UART1 | 15 | 31 |
579: | UART2 | 16 | 32 |
580: | MAILBOX统一ICU source | 63 | 79 |
581: 
582: openvela `bk7258_irq.c`实现：
583: 
584: - `up_irqinitialize()`：关闭所有外部IRQ、设置VTOR、配置默认priority、绑定SVC/HardFault/BusFault/UsageFault/MemFault/SecureFault、最后开启中断。
585: - `up_enable_irq()`：按NVIC ISER或系统异常寄存器开启。
586: - `up_disable_irq()`：按NVIC ICER或系统异常寄存器关闭。
587: - `up_prioritize_irq()`：按NVIC优先级寄存器设置。
588: - `arm_ack_irq()`：NVIC无需单独ack，外设ISR负责清设备pending。
589: 
590: BK7258外部中断不是只配置NVIC即可，必须实现完整三级路径：
591: 
592: ```text
593: 外设中断源
594:   -> 系统控制层将source路由到物理CPU1或CPU2
595:   -> 目标core私有NVIC external line
596:   -> NuttX IRQ编号和ISR
597: ```
598: 
599: 例如mailbox必须完成`source 63 -> CPU1系统路由 -> NVIC line 63 -> NuttX IRQ 79`。只在`irq.h`定义编号不能使中断到达CPU1。进入SMP阶段后，每个外设还必须明确唯一owner或共享路由策略，不能让CPU1和CPU2同时无保护处理同一外设中断；AP日志使用Mailbox UART逻辑通道，不要求CPU1接管物理UART1中断。
600: 
601: 必须在 `include/irq.h` 固化两个编号域，例如 `BK7258_EXTIRQ_MAILBOX=63`、`BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX=BK7258_IRQ_FIRST+63=79`，并设置 `NR_IRQS=80`。`irq_attach()`使用79，NVIC bit和BK gate使用63。`IRQ_MAILBOX0=48`、`IRQ_MAILBOX1=49`等旧header注释不能代替CPU1最终映射。
602: 
603: 还必须区分两套“group”命名：`icu_map.h`中的逻辑group与系统寄存器0-31/32-63 enable bank不是同一概念。mailbox driver实际对source 63调用 `sys_drv_core_intr_group2_enable(..., 1 << (63 - 32))`，即打开32-63 bank的bit31。文档和实现均应使用“32-63 bank”描述寄存器，避免写成含糊的GROUP1。

Cache symbols are internally confusing: `CONFIG_DCACHE/ICACHE` select CMSIS capabilities, while `CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE` controls actual SRAM cacheability and D-cache startup. The shipped AVDK configs have the former set but the latter off, and OpenVela marks AP RAM non-cacheable with DMA disabled, so current FIFO transfer buffers avoid DMA coherency work. I’m doing a final pass over startup/cache code and register comments to enumerate the exact traps that would reappear if DMA or cache is enabled later.

text:
**Executive Finding**
- BK7258’s active SDIO host register base is **secure `0x458d0000`**. The non-secure alias is **`0x558d0000`** because the SDK adds `0x10000000` when `CONFIG_SPE` is false: [reg_base.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:19), [reg_base.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:125). Final AP builds use `CONFIG_SPE=1`, and generated security policy marks SDIO secure and privileged: [_ppc.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/partitions/_build/_ppc.h:134), [tfm_hal_ppc.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/bk7258/armino/partitions/_build/tfm_hal_ppc.h:79).
- The AP SDIO interrupt is **SoC source/NVIC external line 10**. In the current BK7258 NuttX numbering scheme, that derives to **NuttX IRQ/vector 16 + 10 = 26**. It is derivable but **not yet defined or attached** in the current OpenVela port.
- Shipped AVDK `app` and `app_ab` use **one-bit SDIO**, CPU FIFO transfers, initial 100 kHz, then 20 MHz, with SDIO GDMA and PM restore callbacks disabled.
- SDIO protocol/register/IRQ ownership is AP CPU1. Central clock-gate changes are requested by AP and executed by CP. The generic AVDK SD-card LDO is GPIO13 active-high, but this is not universal: the AI/SD-NAND product variant uses GPIO52.

**Registers And HAL**
- Both `bk_idk` and `bk_avdk_smp` define the same base: [IDK reg_base.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:125), [AVDK AP reg_base.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/soc/bk7258/reg_base.h:125). HAL assigns that base to `hal->hw`: [sdio_host_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/sdio_host_hal.c:18), [sdio_ll.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:27).
- Register span shown by generated definitions is at least `0x458d0000` through `0x458d005c`; TX FIFO is `+0x3c`, RX FIFO `+0x40`: [sdio_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_reg.h:325), [sdio_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_reg.h:330).
- Do not use the legacy `middleware/driver/sdcard` base selection for BK7258. It falls through to `0x00802d00`, while only `CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX` selects `0x448b0000`: [sdio_driver.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdcard/sdio_driver.h:22). Final builds select the refactored V2 path.
- Generated comments are stale: early register comments claim `0x448b0000`, although the macro computes from `SOC_SDIO_REG_BASE`: [sdio_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_reg.h:109). There is also a field-definition error where DATA_CRC_OK is `BIT(12)` but its shift is declared 13, the same shift as CRC_FAIL: [sdio_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_reg.h:92). Use the BK7258 TRM or tested LL behavior, not these comments alone.
- Reset semantics contradict each other. LL writes zero while saying reset is low-active: [sdio_ll.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:31). The generated structure says FIFO/state reset is high-active W1C with default 1: [sdio_struct.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sdio_struct.h:154). This needs TRM confirmation or register/clock probing.
- V2 initialization resets SDIO registers before `sdio_host_init_common()` enables the clock: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:559). Driver registration also invokes HAL reset before card-level power-up: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:462), [driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:404). Whether those writes work with the gate off depends on reset clock state and should be measured.

**IRQ And NuttX**
- `INT_SRC_SDIO` is enum ordinal 10: [int_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/int_types.h:98). Both SDK maps route it to external input 10: [AVDK icu_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/icu_map.h:40), [IDK icu_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/icu_map.h:40).
- The AP vector handler dispatches line 10, and ISR registration maps the logical source through `icu_map`: [interrupt.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/bk7258_ap/interrupt.c:165), [interrupt_base.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/icu/interrupt_base.c:37). The SDIO driver installs its ISR at driver initialization: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:482).
- CPU1 system routing uses bit 10 in its `0-31` enable bank: [sys_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sys_reg.h:1116). AP `sys_hal_int_enable()` writes the CPU1 route register unconditionally: [sys_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sys_hal.c:571).
- Current NuttX defines `BK7258_IRQ_FIRST=16`, 64 external lines, and `NR_IRQS=80`, but has no SDIO symbol: [irq.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/include/irq.h:24). Its generic routing code supports line 10 and routes it to CPU1: [bk7258_irq.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c:27), [bk7258_irq.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_irq.c:145). Therefore prospective definitions are `BK7258_EXTIRQ_SDIO=10` and `BK7258_IRQ_SDIO=26`.
- The runtime table has a real entry at vector 26: [bk7258_vectors.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_vectors.c:41). Current final NuttX config has MMC/SD and DMA disabled: [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:659), [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:810).
- `ICU_PRI_IRQ_SDIO=22` is an unused legacy constant, not the AP external line or NuttX vector: [icu_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/icu_reg.h:106). No source references it outside the definition.

**Clock, Power And Reset**
- Hardware init enables `CLK_PWR_ID_SDIO`, selects source 0 as XTAL 26 MHz, enables route bit 10, and enables SDIO masks: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:320).
- Clock control is register `SYSCTRL+0x30`, bit 22; source/divider are `SYSCTRL+0x24`, bits 17 and 14-16: [sys_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sys_reg.h:271), [sys_reg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/sys_reg.h:344).
- AP `sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up()` is actually a PM mailbox request: [sys_clock_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sys_ctrl/sys_clock_driver.c:22), [pm.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_pm/pm.c:1389). CP handles that request and writes the central gate: [low_pwr_core.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/low_pwr_core.c:228), [CP sys_clock_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/sys_ctrl/sys_clock_driver.c:20), [CP sys_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sys_hal.c:1010).
- Final AP starts card identification at enum 7 = 100 kHz, then selects enum 14 = 20 MHz: [hal_sdio_host_types.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/hal/hal_sdio_host_types.h:25), [sd_card_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sd_card/sd_card_driver.c:983), [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1124).
- Clock programming is a hard-coded write to secure `0x44010024`, not `SOC_SYS_REG_BASE`; it is unsuitable unchanged for a non-secure build: [sdio_ll.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/sdio_ll.h:92).
- No distinct top-level SDIO reset is used. Only clock gating plus FIFO/SD state reset is visible. The HAL itself warns that clock and power are separate on this generation, but the final build disables `SDIO_PM_CB_SUPPORT` and BAKP power-domain PM control: [CP sys_hal.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sys_hal.c:1010), [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1151). Confirm BAKP reset/default power state in the TRM or by reading the power-status and clock registers.

**Signals And External Power**
- Generic final `app/app_ab`: GPIO2=CLK, GPIO3=CMD, GPIO4=DATA0, all pull-up and drive capacity 3: [app usr_gpio_cfg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/usr_gpio_cfg.h:26). One-bit and lower pin group are selected: [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1127), [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1136).
- Alternate complete banks are GPIO2/3/4/5/10/11 or GPIO14-19: [gpio_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:181). Four-bit lower-bank mode conflicts with CP’s GPIO5 interrupt and GPIO10/11 UART0: [CP usr_gpio_cfg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/usr_gpio_cfg.h:23). GPIO14-19 conflicts with the generic AP LCD map.
- AVDK AP’s map checks undefined `CONFIG_PIN_SDIO_GROUP_0`, while Kconfig and IDK use `CONFIG_PIN_SDIO_GROUP_1`: [AVDK gpio_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:191), [Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/Kconfig:14), [IDK gpio_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/gpio_map.h:192). Project user GPIO tables mask this bug in current builds, but dynamic pin selection should be corrected or verified.
- Generic AVDK defines SD-card LDO as `CONFIG_LDO3V3_CTRL_GPIO`, final GPIO13 active-high: [gpio_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:453), [generated sdkconfig.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/bk7258/app/bk7258_ap/config/sdkconfig.h:276). FATFS drives it high before card init and votes sleep off: [disk_io.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/fatfs/disk_io.c:58), [disk_io.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/fatfs/disk_io.c:194). Automatic idle power-down is disabled.
- GPIO13 is not proven to be “SD NAND power” universally: it is also aliased as motor LDO, and AVDK documentation uses GPIO13 for LCD LDO. `app_ab` initially configures GPIO13 as a falling-edge input before the SD-card path forcibly unmaps it as output: [gpio_map.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h:456), [app_ab usr_gpio_cfg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/ap/config/bk7258_ap/usr_gpio_cfg.h:34), [pm_ap_misc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_misc.c:435).
- The documented 128 MB SD-NAND “Beken Genie” board instead maps SDIO to GPIO14-19 and uses GPIO52 for 3.3 V enable: [README.md](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_solution_ai/projects/beken_genie/README.md:53), [usr_gpio_cfg.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_solution_ai/projects/beken_genie/ap/config/bk7258_ap/usr_gpio_cfg.h:36), [config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_solution_ai/projects/beken_genie/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1536), [ap_main.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_solution_ai/projects/beken_genie/ap/ap_main.c:144). Board revision/schematic identity is therefore mandatory.

**Cache, DMA And Ownership**
- Final AVDK has D/I-cache capability enabled and startup enables D-cache, but `CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLE` is off and MPU maps shared SRAM and PSRAM non-cacheable; peripheral space is Device memory: [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1034), [startup_cpu0.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/cmsis/CMSIS_5/Device/Beken/bk7236xx/Source/smp/startup_cpu0.c:376), [mpu_cfg.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/mpu_cfg.c:101).
- SDIO GDMA is disabled, so transfers poll/copy FIFO from the CPU: [app config](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app/ap/config/bk7258_ap/config:1149), [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:946), [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:1199).
- Future GDMA enablement needs work: SDIO declares buffers as `DMA_DEV_DTCM` regardless of actual pointer location, changes addresses per transfer without cache maintenance, and generic DMA only flushes addresses present at channel initialization: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:197), [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:238), [dma_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/general_dma/dma_driver.c:327). TX requires clean-before-DMA; RX requires invalidate/ownership barriers after DMA. Alignment also needs enforcement because CPU writes cast buffers to `uint32_t *`: [sdio_host_driver.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/sdio_host/sdio_host_driver.c:975).
- Peripheral ownership is explicitly AP-facing in vendor documentation: [resource documentation](/home/mi/vela_competition/博通网页文档/外设资源介绍%20—%20博通集成%20ARMINO%20SMP开发框架%20文档.html:242). Final CP configs contain no SDIO/SD-card symbols, while final AP configs enable both. AP CPU1 owns the IRQ route and controller state; CP owns execution of central clock requests. Do not initialize the host from CP or AP CPU2 concurrently.
- Current NuttX is secure, single-core, has non-cacheable AP RAM, and no MMCSD/SDIO lower half: [defconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:16), [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:404). Porting requires a new BK7258 `sdio_dev_s`, IRQ26 definition/attach, CPU1 route bit10, GPIO/LDO board hooks, and MMCSD binding.

No files were written or modified.
